paper_title: 1+12 Can Large Language Models Serve as Cross-Lingual Knowledge   Aggregators
caption: Statistics of the dataset in our experiments.
model_annotation: This 3D pie chart illustrates the statistics of a dataset used in an experiment, displaying its distribution across five distinct categories. The chart does not include a separate legend; instead, text labels are positioned outside the pie with thin lines pointing to their corresponding slices, detailing the category name, percentage, and absolute count in parentheses. The largest segment is a red slice labeled "TriviaQA," which accounts for 46% (1829) of the total and is visually exploded, or offset, from the main body of the chart. Adjacent to it is another exploded yellow slice labeled "Chinese Domain," representing 6% (231). The remaining three contiguous slices consist of a green segment labeled "HalluEval" at 18% (721), a light blue segment labeled "HalluQA" at 5% (185), and a purple segment labeled "WebQA" at 25% (997). Visually, the segments are not arranged in a strict ascending or descending sequence based on their proportions.
